findings.evidence: `pkg/executor/internal/exec/executor.go:60` documents `Close()` may run concurrently with `Next()`. In this commit, parallel-hashagg spill files are only registered into the helper in the fetcher goroutine defer: `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:420`-`440` (notably `addListInDisks` at `pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:428`-`435`). Cleanup in `Close()` only calls `spillHelper.close()` (`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:209`-`213`), which closes only `spillHelper.lock.spilledChunksIO` (`pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_spill.go:107`-`115`). If `Close()` happens before the fetcher defer runs and registers `partialWorkers[i].spilledChunksIO`, those `DataInDiskByChunks` can remain open/unremoved.
findings.fix:
Make spill-file cleanup robust to `Close()` racing with `fetchChildData()`:
- Option A: ensure `Close()` waits for the fetcher goroutine to finish its defer (or at least for spill-file registration) before calling `spillHelper.close()`.
- Option B: in `Close()`, also close any `partialWorkers[i].spilledChunksIO` that exist (being careful to avoid double-closing; may require making `DataInDiskByChunks.Close()` idempotent or clearing references after closing).
- Option C: in `fetchChildData` defer, if `finishCh` is closed (cancellation), close spilled `DataInDiskByChunks` directly instead of relying on `Close()` after registration.
findings.impact: On canceled/early-closed queries where parallel hash-agg spill has created temp files, TiDB can leak temporary spill files and file descriptors (and associated disk usage). This can accumulate under repeated cancellations/timeouts and lead to temp-dir disk exhaustion or FD pressure, impacting cluster stability.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943` (2026-03-20): `addListInDisks` still happens in `fetchChildData` defer (`upstream/master:pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:465`-`474`), while `Close()` still calls `spillHelper.close()` (`upstream/master:pkg/executor/aggregate/agg_hash_executor.go:205`-`238`). No synchronization/cleanup was found that guarantees spill files registered after `Close()` are closed.
findings.verify: Repro-style validation (no tests required): run a query that triggers parallel hash-agg spill (low `tidb_mem_quota_query`, ensure tmp-storage-on-OOM path enabled), then cancel/kill the query mid-execution so `Close()` runs before normal completion. Observe whether spill temp files remain under TiDB temp dir and whether `StmtCtx.DiskTracker`/OS disk usage does not drop after cancellation.
findings.what: Parallel hash-agg spill temp files may leak on early `Close()` (query cancel/timeout) because `Close()` can run concurrently with the fetcher goroutine and closes only spill files already registered in `spillHelper`; registration happens later in `fetchChildData` defer, and there is no guaranteed post-registration cleanup.
